creatures.name: Basilisk

archive.food: Fertilized Rock Drake Egg / Fertilized Magmasaur Egg / Fertilized Wyvern Egg / Fertilized Voidwyrm Egg
archive.notes: Drop compatible fertilized eggs from the survivor inventory near an emerged Basilisk and give it space to consume them. Dropping from a mount inventory can consume an egg without tame progress. Prepare poison protection, safe positioning and extra eggs rather than treating it as a knockout tame.

creatures.updateNote: Exact food counts, tame times and base stats are not verified.

creatures.name: Bulbdog

archive.notes: Put tame food in the last hotbar slot and hand-feed when hungry. Protect it from nearby enemies rather than shooting tranquilizers. After taming, manage its charge light: the light helps against Nameless/Reapers but can attract Seekers; switch it off safely to recharge.

creatures.updateNote: Exact food counts, tame times and base stats are not verified.

creatures.name: Cosmo

archive.notes: Carry Chitin and approach a landed Cosmo only while its light is green. Stop moving when it turns red; advancing then can provoke webs and flight. Feed at the green opportunity and repeat the approach as it moves away. Plant Species Z Seed provides more tame progress than Chitin.

creatures.updateNote: Base stats, tame times and exact supply quantities are not verified in this profile.

archive.food: Plant Species Z Seed / Auric Mushroom
archive.notes: Aerial charge light pet. Wider light radius than Bulbdog.

creatures.name: Glowtail

archive.food: Plant Species Z Seed / Ascerbic Mushroom
archive.notes: Use passive hand-feeding with food in the last hotbar slot. Feeding can fail while it is in water, so choose a dry safe position. Its light is useful protection but attracts Seekers; allow recharge while switched off and keep this small pet out of combat.

creatures.updateNote: Exact food counts, tame times and base stats are not verified.

archive.food: Exceptional Kibble / Spoiled Meat / Raw Meat
archive.notes: Aberration's premier gather/combat mount. Climbs walls, harvests most resources, and carries platforms.

creatures.name: Lamprey

archive.notes: Use a Fish Basket to capture it rather than food taming. Its hostile attachment behavior can break the basket or cause escape, and a captured Lamprey does not act like a normal companion. Wild attachment drains health while providing temporary charge/radiation utility; PvE/PvP rules affect later attachment use.

creatures.updateNote: Base stats, tame times and exact supply counts are not verified.

creatures.name: Glowbug

archive.notes: Interact for charge-light utility rather than trying to tame it. It flees when attacked. This wild utility creature is not a tameable shoulder light pet.

creatures.updateNote: No fabricated food or resource-drop values.

creatures.name: Nameless

archive.notes: Prepare a charged light pet before entering hostile underground regions. Nameless can emerge without warning when charge light is absent, including near foundations. Deal with persistent groups promptly: prolonged encounters can escalate into a Reaper threat. Camouflage alone is not reliable protection.

creatures.updateNote: Base stats, tame times and exact supply counts are not verified.

creatures.name: Ravager

archive.notes: Isolate the target from its pack before taming. A Bola helps control the chosen Ravager while you knock it out, but its packmates can interrupt or increase danger. Keep food and torpor supplies ready after the knockout.

creatures.updateNote: Base stats, tame times and exact supply quantities are not verified in this profile.

creatures.name: Reaper Queen

archive.notes: An adult Queen cannot be tamed. The offspring route involves survivor impregnation and raising a Reaper King; it is not a Queen knockout tame. Prepare the map-specific conditions and a safe nursery before attempting the offspring route.

creatures.updateNote: Adult and offspring status are deliberately separated. No unverified impregnation HP threshold or variant stats copied.

creatures.name: Rock Drake
creatures.method: Wild egg hatch · adults not directly tameable

archive.method: Wild egg hatch · adults not directly tameable
archive.notes: Acquire and hatch a wild egg rather than knocking out an adult. Prepare hazard protection where the nesting route is irradiated, plan your escape before stealing, and verify current ASA incubation and juvenile feeding requirements before committing. Climbing and gliding make it useful transport after raising.

creatures.updateNote: Base stats, tame times and exact supply quantities are not verified in this profile.

creatures.name: Roll Rat

archive.notes: Wait for an actual burrow, then throw Giant Bee Honey into the hole. Repeat on later burrows; a digging animation that only unearths food is not the feeding window. Avoid cliffs and protect your honey supply, since thrown honey cannot be retrieved.

creatures.updateNote: Base stats, tame times and exact supply quantities are not verified in this profile.

creatures.name: Seeker

archive.notes: Charge light attracts and strengthens Seekers. When fighting them, assess whether turning off a light source is safe: it weakens Seekers but can expose you to Nameless. Keep your travel and recharge plan ready rather than using a light pet as unconditional protection.

creatures.updateNote: Base stats, tame times and exact supply counts are not verified.

archive.food: Plant Species Z Seed / Aggeravic Mushroom / Sweet Vegetable Cake
archive.notes: Aberration shoulder pet. Emits charge light to repel Nameless. Longer charge duration than Glowtail.

creatures.name: Surface Reaper King

archive.notes: This hostile surface variant is not the offspring route from a Reaper Queen. Prepare charge light to weaken its protection and avoid fighting beside hazardous drops or Element water because tail attacks can knock you away. Have an exit plan from the surface as daylight approaches.

creatures.updateNote: Base stats, tame times and exact supply counts are not verified.

creatures.name: Yi Ling

archive.notes: Ordinary tranquilizers do not add torpor. Survive its feather attacks, stun it with Plant Species Z Fruit during the dive window, then use the torpor-feeding interaction with Bio Toxin. Once knocked out, feed taming food. Bring spare armor and healing; timing is the main challenge.

creatures.updateNote: ASA-specific procedure; Plant Species Z Fruit is distinct from the seed. No exact feather/feed count or stat target copied.
